correctness.rationale: The characteristic-two linear change produces the cubic cone over smooth S. Every line is a cone ruling or lies in the plane over a line on S, giving all 28 two-dimensional supports; the rank-four cubic section on the smooth six-dimensional Grassmannian makes its pure codimension-four zero locus locally complete intersection with no embedded components. At a general ruling the four coefficient equations eliminate a smooth base coordinate and one tangent-normal variable and leave binary homogeneous forms of degrees 2 and 3, with no common projective root by the absence of S-lines through the chosen P. Hence their quotient length is 6. In characteristic two the quadratic is a square geometrically, and a coordinate change reduces the cubic modulo the square to v^3, giving geometric generic transverse ring kbar[[u,v]]/(u^2,v^3). For generic lines inside cone planes, the normal sequence with N_(ell/S)=O(-1) implies tangent dimension 2 and generic reducedness. The Plucker degrees 3 and 1 yield total 45. Standalone GF2, GF4, GF256 exact field calculations reproduce 27 lines and a nondegenerate generic ruling witness but are explicitly not the infinite proof.

originality.rationale: The 2015 Dolgachev primary full text, particularly Section 4 on Fano surfaces, describes 6 del Pezzo components and 15 planar components of the characteristic-zero Segre cubic. It does not supply the characteristic-two length-six nonreduced ruling component or the associated 28-component cycle. The characteristic-two cubic-surface full text of Kadyrsizova et al., especially its introduction, Section 4, and Theorem 5.1, concerns the cubic surface and line configuration, not the line Fano scheme of a cone over it. Previously studied cone constructions with different base varieties do not imply this specific cubic-surface transverse (2,3) complete intersection. Novelty is provisional; unpublished or unindexed equivalent stronger results are an acknowledged residual risk.
